name: Pierre Robin Syndrome Associated with Branchial Arch Anomalies
aliases: Pierre Robin Sequence with Branchial Arch Defects
Pierre Robin Syndrome with Branchial Arch Malformations

criteria.description: U-shaped cleft palate or other palatal anomalies
Presence of branchial arch anomalies such as branchial clefts or fistulas
Neonatal respiratory distress due to upper airway obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of micrognathia, glossoptosis, and cleft palate
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Branchial arch anomalies support the diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Small mandible is a hallmark feature
Posterior displacement of the tongue causing airway obstruction

common.notes: External neck anomalies related to branchial arch defects
Secondary to cleft palate and airway obstruction
Middle ear infections common due to eustachian tube dysfunction

occasional.notes: Conductive hearing loss related to middle ear anomalies
Including hypoplasia of hyoid bone or other skeletal elements
Due to branchial arch developmental defects
Secondary to feeding difficulties and airway obstruction
searchTerms: recurrent pneumonia due to inhaled food or liquids

rare.notes: Occasional association with branchial arch syndromes
May occur secondary to hypoxia or syndromic associations

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; supportive labs to rule out infections or complications
imaging: Lateral neck ultrasound or MRI to identify branchial cleft cysts or fistulas
Craniofacial CT scan showing micrognathia and cleft palate
Chest X-ray to assess aspiration pneumonia
genetic: No single gene identified; may be sporadic or part of syndromic presentations involving branchial arch development genes
other: Airway endoscopy to evaluate glossoptosis and airway obstruction

distinguishingFeatures: No glossoptosis or airway obstruction as primary feature
Cleft palate without branchial arch anomalies

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress requiring airway intervention
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
references: Robin P. Sur une anomalie de la machoire inferieure (micrognathie) accompagnée d'une fente palatine et d'une glossoptose. Bull Soc Med Hop Paris. 1923.
Orphanet Report on Pierre Robin Syndrome Associated with Branchial Arch Anomalies, ORPHA:138050.
Jones KL. Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation. 7th ed. 2013.
